name: Cyathus striatus
notes: A brown mat that binds debris (the survey codes it CORD/LIT). Raindrops splash the "eggs" out at 67 to 73 degrees and up to 1 m (research/05 [22]); each egg is reported (unchecked) to trail a sticky cord that wraps around a stem.

tip_speed.note: Claude's inference from the species' ecology and general knowledge, not from a measurement (2026-11-10): colonises mulch and woody debris quickly; set above the family default

uptake_rate.note: tuning value, set to tip speed / segment length so that one feeding segment can supply about one growing tip; no measurement found
